title: The Effect of Problem-Based Learning on Students’ Environmental Literacy: A Meta-Analysis
text_snippet: The Effect of Problem-Based Learning on Students’ Environmental Literacy: A Meta-Analysis Environmental literacy is essential for enabling students to understand environmental problems and make responsible decisions. This study aimed to estimate the overall effect of Problem-Based Learning (PBL) on students’ environmental literacy knowledge and to examine variation across included studies. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using eight experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between 2018 and 2025. Studies were identified through Google Scholar using Publish or Perish and selected according to criteria requiring experimental and control groups, post-test means, standard deviations, and sample sizes. Effect sizes were calculated using Hedges’ g under a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was examined using Cochran’s Q, tau-squared, and I-squared statistics, while potential publication bias was assessed through funnel-plot inspection. The pooled effect size was large and statistically significant (Hedges’ g = 0.86, 95% CI [0.37, 1.36], p = .005), indicating that PBL improved students’ environmental literacy knowledge compared with non-PBL instruction. title: Futures Thinking for Culturally Grounded Problem-Solving: Reimagining Sustainable Bali Tourism through Local Knowledge
text_snippet: Futures Thinking for Culturally Grounded Problem-Solving: Reimagining Sustainable Bali Tourism through Local Knowledge Students’ limited creative thinking and problem-solving skills require higher education to develop pedagogical approaches that are future-oriented, contextual, and culturally grounded. This study explored how a futures thinking approach deepened university students’ engagement with local knowledge and strengthened their problem-solving skills through the “Future Bali Travel in 2034” project. A qualitative action research design was employed with ten pre-service teacher education students at Universitas Pendidikan Ganesha. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, reflective notes, learning artifacts, and student project outputs, then analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings showed that students developed a broader understanding of futures thinking as a way to imagine alternative futures, anticipate change, and design adaptive responses. Students also reinterpreted Balinese local knowledge as a living resource for sustainable tourism innovation. Project outputs demonstrated students’ ability to integrate cultural preservation, digital innovation, environmental awareness, and community empowerment into future tourism scenarios. title: Sustainable Development Goals-Based Digital Comics for Enhancing Primary Students’ English Reading Literacy: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Sustainable Development Goals-Based Digital Comics for Enhancing Primary Students’ English Reading Literacy: A Systematic Literature Review Reading literacy remains a persistent challenge in primary education, particularly because students often show low reading interest and limited engagement with conventional reading materials. This study aims to examine the characteristics, advantages, and challenges of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)-based digital comics for students’ English literacy in primary schools. A library research design was employed by adapting George’s research procedure, which involved topic determination, research question formulation, source selection, article screening, data reduction, synthesis, and reporting. Twenty-nine articles from reputable national and international indexed journals were analyzed thematically. The findings reveal that SDG-based digital comics have three main characteristics: visual attractiveness, ease of use and access, and relevance to 21st-century learning. The reviewed studies also show that this medium supports vocabulary mastery, reading comprehension, communication skills, writing skills, learning outcomes, literacy competence, and digital literacy. title: Beyond the Label “C4”: Profiling Pre-Service Elementary Teachers’ Analytical Thinking in Mathematical Problem-Solving Using Anderson & Krathwohl’s Bloom’s Taxonomy in Online Learning
text_snippet: Beyond the Label “C4”: Profiling Pre-Service Elementary Teachers’ Analytical Thinking in Mathematical Problem-Solving Using Anderson & Krathwohl’s Bloom’s Taxonomy in Online Learning Anderson and Krathwohl’s revised Bloom’s Taxonomy classifies students’ cognitive level, but a label such as “analyzing” does not by itself explain how students who reach that level actually reason. This study examined 68 pre-service elementary teachers’ (PGSD students) responses to a composite-area geometry problem administered in an online learning environment, coding all responses against the taxonomy’s six cognitive levels and then inductively profiling the analytical reasoning of students who reached the analyzing (C4) level. Only 7 students (10.3%) reached C4; the remaining 61 (89.7%) became stuck at applying, understanding, or remembering. Close reading of the seven successful responses, triangulated with interviews, revealed three distinguishable analysis profiles — relational, procedural, and visual — each grounded in established constructs of mathematical reasoning. A conceptual model, Apply→Transition→Analyze, is proposed to describe the cognitive transition zone in which most students became stuck. title: How Do Teachers’ Experience and School Location Influence Joyful Teaching in Geography Education?
text_snippet: How Do Teachers’ Experience and School Location Influence Joyful Teaching in Geography Education? Quantitative evidence on joyful teaching in subject-specific contexts remains limited, particularly in education systems characterized by spatial disparities in resources. This study examined the effects of school location, teaching experience, and their interaction on joyful teaching practices among geography teachers in East Java, Indonesia. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design was employed. Participants comprised 50 geography teachers from 50 senior high schools located in cities and regencies. Data were collected using the Joyful Teaching Self-Reflection Scale, adapted from the Learning Enjoyment Scale, which demonstrated acceptable internal consistency with Cronbach’s α of 0.745 and McDonald’s ω of 0.764. title: Exploring the Implementation of Mathematics Lesson Study in the Diploma in Primary Education Course in Bangladesh: Challenges and Opportunities
text_snippet: Exploring the Implementation of Mathematics Lesson Study in the Diploma in Primary Education Course in Bangladesh: Challenges and Opportunities Persistent reliance on teacher-centred mathematics instruction limits conceptual learning and maintains a gap between reform-oriented teacher preparation and classroom practice. This study examined Lesson Study implementation within the mathematics component of the Diploma in Primary Education programme, focusing on trainee teachers’ understanding, instructional enactment, and reflective practice. A qualitative-dominant concurrent embedded mixed-methods design was conducted over six months. Nine trainee teachers from two Primary Teacher Training Institutes and two instructors were selected purposively. Data were collected through semi-structured questionnaires, analysis of 27 lesson plans, video-recorded observations of 18 research lessons, and audio-recorded post-lesson reflections. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, while qualitative data were examined using deductive and inductive thematic analysis and integrated through triangulation. Findings showed stronger procedural than conceptual understanding of Lesson Study. title: Who Values Education? Socio-Demographic Predictors of Educational Attitudes in the Philippines
text_snippet: Who Values Education? Socio-Demographic Predictors of Educational Attitudes in the Philippines Educational equity requires attention not only to formal access but also to social values that shape how families and communities perceive educational opportunity. This study examined socio-demographic predictors of educational values in the Philippines, focusing on concern about providing quality education for children and agreement with the belief that university education is more important for boys than for girls. A quantitative cross-sectional design was applied using secondary data from the World Values Survey Wave 7 Philippines. The study analyzed a weighted sample of 1,200 adult respondents selected through a multi-stage probability sampling design across major Philippine regions. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression. The findings showed that 11.2% of respondents expressed serious concern about providing quality education, while 44% agreed that university education is more important for boys. Bivariate analysis indicated significant associations between educational concern and marital status, age, and religion. title: From Knowledge Acquisition to Competency Development: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Approaches in Science Education
text_snippet: From Knowledge Acquisition to Competency Development: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Approaches in Science Education Science education requires a pedagogical shift from knowledge transmission toward competency development that prepares students for complex twenty-first-century challenges. This study systematically reviewed the implementation of deep learning approaches in science education and their contribution to students’ twenty-first-century skills. The review followed the PRISMA framework through identification, screening, eligibility assessment, and inclusion. Searches conducted in Scopus and Google Scholar identified 505 records published between 2016 and 2025, of which 19 articles met the inclusion criteria. Data were extracted according to publication year, country, educational level, instructional strategy, targeted competencies, and principal findings. Results showed a clear increase in publications, with Indonesia contributing the largest number of studies and higher education representing the dominant research setting. title: Exploring the Effect of Quizizz-Based Learning and Learning Facilities on Academic Achievement: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation
text_snippet: Exploring the Effect of Quizizz-Based Learning and Learning Facilities on Academic Achievement: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation This study was motivated by the need to clarify how gamified learning, learning facilities, and learning motivation interact in shaping students’ academic achievement. The study aimed to examine the direct effects of Quizizz-based learning and learning facilities on academic achievement and to analyze the mediating role of learning motivation. An explanatory quantitative approach with a causal-correlational design was employed. The participants were 250 students of Muhammadiyah PK Junior High School Surakarta selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire measuring Quizizz-based learning, learning facilities, learning motivation, and academic achievement. The data were analyzed using Exploratory Factor Analysis, Confirmatory Factor Analysis, Structural Equation Modeling, and bootstrapping. The findings showed that Quizizz-based learning significantly affected learning motivation but did not directly affect academic achievement. Learning facilities significantly affected both learning motivation and academic achievement. title: Cooperative Integrated Reading and Composition for Elementary Reading Comprehension: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Cooperative Integrated Reading and Composition for Elementary Reading Comprehension: A Systematic Literature Review Elementary students’ reading comprehension remains a persistent literacy problem because many learners can read texts but struggle to identify main ideas, interpret information, draw conclusions, and summarize content. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Cooperative Integrated Reading and Composition (CIRC) learning model in improving elementary school students’ reading comprehension through a systematic literature review. Reading comprehension is a fundamental literacy skill that supports students’ ability to understand subject matter, process information, and participate actively in learning. This study reviewed articles published from 2019 to 2023 using Google Scholar as the database. The search used the keywords “CIRC learning model,” “improve the ability,” “reading comprehension of students,” and “elementary school.” Article selection was conducted through screening of titles, abstracts, full texts, citation relevance, and accessibility. Ten articles met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using descriptive and thematic synthesis. title: A Phenomenological Exploration of Job Satisfaction among Primary School Teachers in Khulna, Bangladesh
text_snippet: A Phenomenological Exploration of Job Satisfaction among Primary School Teachers in Khulna, Bangladesh The quality of education and student learning outcomes are significantly influenced by primary school teacher job satisfaction, yet limited evidence exists on the contextual factors influencing teachers' satisfaction in Khulna, Bangladesh. The objective is to identify the factors affecting job satisfaction among primary-level school teachers in Khulna and to understand their actual experiences within the educational system. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed, using purposive sampling to select 30 primary school teachers from government and non-government institutions. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, and data were analyzed following Braun and Clarke’s six-step thematic analysis. The results found five major themes: compensation challenges, limited professional development opportunities, variations in administrative support, inadequate classroom resources and infrastructure, and differing levels of community recognition, which together illustrate how teachers’ job satisfaction is shaped by the interaction of financial, institutional, material, and social conditions. title: The Reflection of Merdeka Curriculum Research to Inform the New Policy: A Bibliometric Analysis of Indonesian Higher Education (2020–2025)
text_snippet: The Reflection of Merdeka Curriculum Research to Inform the New Policy: A Bibliometric Analysis of Indonesian Higher Education (2020–2025) Indonesia’s transition from Merdeka Belajar Kampus Merdeka (MBKM) toward Kampus Berdampak creates a need to examine the scholarly legacy of the previous policy and its relevance for future higher education reform. This study aims to map the development of MBKM scholarship from 2020 to 2025 through publication trends, citation performance, influential works, active authors, and co-authorship structures. A bibliometric design was applied using records retrieved from Scopus and Google Scholar. From 1,220 initial records, 686 publications met the screening criteria and were analyzed using Publish or Perish and VOSviewer. The findings show that publication output increased rapidly from 2020 and peaked in 2022 with 184 papers, while the highest citation performance occurred in 2021 with 4,859 citations and 54.60 citations per paper. Highly cited publications were dominated by conceptual and early implementation studies, indicating the strong formative role of foundational MBKM scholarship. title: Understanding Parental Involvement as a Correlate of Students’ Academic Achievement: A Case Study in a National High School
text_snippet: Understanding Parental Involvement as a Correlate of Students’ Academic Achievement: A Case Study in a National High School Limited parental involvement in academic activities may affect students’ motivation, learning responsibility, and academic achievement. This study aimed to examine parental involvement as a correlate of Senior High School students’ academic achievement at Trinidad Mapa-Gupana National High School, Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, Philippines. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 147 respondents consisting of students, parents, and Senior High School teachers across three academic years. Data were collected using researcher-developed questionnaires and teacher open-ended questions, then analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, Chi-square, Pearson correlation, Spearman’s rho, and Cramér’s V. The findings showed that parents demonstrated high involvement in homework supervision and school activities but low involvement in communicating expectations and setting academic goals. title: Accessible Science Learning for Deaf Students in Inclusive Elementary Classrooms: Teaching Strategies, Communication Barriers, and Support Needs
text_snippet: Accessible Science Learning for Deaf Students in Inclusive Elementary Classrooms: Teaching Strategies, Communication Barriers, and Support Needs Deaf students in inclusive elementary schools often experience barriers in science learning because verbal explanations, abstract concepts, and science terminology are not always accessible through conventional classroom practices. This study aimed to describe the science learning process for deaf students at SD Inklusi Negeri 2 Bengkala, focusing on teaching strategies, learning challenges, media use, classroom interaction, and the role of the special mentor teacher. A descriptive qualitative design was employed. Data were collected through classroom observation, semi-structured interviews, and document study involving regular teachers, special mentor teachers, hearing students, and deaf students. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings showed that science learning was implemented through expository teaching, contextual learning, demonstration, role-play, visual media, and sign-language assistance. title: Brainstorming in the STEM-integrated Project-based Learning: Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Brainstorming in the STEM-integrated Project-based Learning: Systematic Literature Review STEM-integrated project-based learning (PjBL) has become an important approach in modern education, but its implementation often faces challenges such as a lack of student creativity and collaboration. This phenomenon encourages the importance of research on the role of brainstorming methods in improving the effectiveness of PjBL-STEM. The purpose of this study is to analyze empirical evidence regarding the benefits of brainstorming in the context of PjBL-STEM and to identify challenges and solutions for its implementation. This study uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method with a systematic analysis design on 40 selected articles from 175 initial articles obtained from Scopus, Google Scholar, and ERIC databases. The sample was selected based on inclusion criteria such as relevance, full-text availability, and publications in the last 10 years (2014–2024). The research instruments included the SLR protocol, the CASP evaluation tool, and network analysis using VOSviewer. title: Adaptation and Innovation: The Impact of Learning Models on Effective Integration of Emerging Technologies
text_snippet: Adaptation and Innovation: The Impact of Learning Models on Effective Integration of Emerging Technologies Educational institutions still face difficulties integrating emerging technologies meaningfully because digital tools are often adopted without adaptive learning models that guide pedagogical use. This study aims to examine how learning models support the effective integration of emerging technologies in educational settings. A systematic literature review was employed by synthesizing scholarly articles, books, book chapters, and empirical studies related to learning models, digital learning environments, adaptive pedagogy, and technology integration. The findings show that technology integration becomes more effective when supported by student-centred, collaborative, inclusive, and assessment-oriented learning models. Behaviourist and cognitivist models support structured practice and cognitive scaffolding, while constructivist, connectivist, blended, flipped, inquiry-based, project-based, and gamified learning models provide broader opportunities for engagement, autonomy, collaboration, and critical thinking. title: Academic Stress, Mental Health Symptoms, and Coping Strategies among University Students: Evidence from Khulna University, Bangladesh
text_snippet: Academic Stress, Mental Health Symptoms, and Coping Strategies among University Students: Evidence from Khulna University, Bangladesh Academic stress has become an important concern in higher education because persistent academic demands may coincide with psychological distress and ineffective coping. This study examined the prevalence and sources of academic stress, its associations with depression and anxiety symptoms, coping strategies, and demographic differences among undergraduate students at Khulna University, Bangladesh. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted from January to April 2024 with 366 students recruited through convenience sampling. Academic stress, depression, anxiety, and coping were assessed using a modified Academic Stress Scale, PHQ-9, GAD-7, and Brief COPE. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical multiple regression were applied. Excessive assignment pressure was reported by 82.0% of students, while 34.7% reported depressive symptoms and 28.7% reported anxiety symptoms. Social support was the most frequently used coping strategy (59.8%). Fourth-year students experienced significantly higher academic stress than students in earlier years. title: Effectiveness of Management Information Systems in Elementary Schools: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Effectiveness of Management Information Systems in Elementary Schools: A Systematic Literature Review The effectiveness of Management Information Systems (MIS) in elementary schools has become an important issue as educational governance increasingly requires efficient, accurate, transparent, and data-based management. This study aims to systematically examine the effectiveness of MIS implementation in elementary schools and identify its supporting factors, barriers, and implications for educational service quality. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method was employed by following the PRISMA stages, including identification, screening, eligibility assessment, and article inclusion. A total of 22 scientific articles published between 2020 and 2025 were analyzed thematically based on implementation focus, effectiveness, supporting factors, barriers, and the impacts of MIS. The findings show that MIS plays a positive role in improving administrative efficiency, data management accuracy, reporting transparency, internal school coordination, and communication between schools and parents. title: Global Patterns and Regional Disparities in Green Curriculum Adoption: A Systematic Review of SDG Integration in Higher Education
text_snippet: Global Patterns and Regional Disparities in Green Curriculum Adoption: A Systematic Review of SDG Integration in Higher Education Global efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have encouraged higher education institutions to embed sustainability principles into curriculum design and implementation. Nevertheless, Green Curriculum adoption remains uneven across regions, and comparative evidence regarding its global development is still fragmented. This study examined publication trends, geographical distribution, innovation patterns, and institutional challenges related to Green Curriculum and SDG integration in higher education from 2015 to 2025. A Systematic Literature Review combined with a scoping review approach was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 framework. Data were collected from Scopus, ERIC, and ScienceDirect, resulting in 113 eligible peer-reviewed articles. Descriptive analysis, thematic synthesis, and bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer were applied to identify research growth, regional contributions, intellectual structures, and implementation pathways. The findings reveal two dominant patterns: technology-driven approaches in developed countries and community-based approaches in developing countries. title: Key Factors that Strengthen Student Entrepreneurial Intention: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Key Factors that Strengthen Student Entrepreneurial Intention: A Systematic Literature Review Entrepreneurial intention among students is increasingly important to reduce the unemployment rate and increase economic growth. The literature review article Key Factors that Strengthen the Entrepreneurial Intention of Students is a research article that aims to find factors that strengthen students' intention in entrepreneurship. The research method used is library research, including searches through Scopus, Harzing's Publish, and Perish. This study uses a comprehensive literature analysis method to evaluate factors such as entrepreneurship education, environmental support (family, friends, and university), practical experience, personal characteristics, and motivation and attitude toward risk. The results show that entrepreneurship education received on campus, access to resources and mentor support, and individual characteristics such as self-confidence and risk-taking courage are the main factors driving students' entrepreneurial intentions. In addition, internal motivation factors and social support also play an essential role in influencing students' decision to choose an entrepreneurial path. title: Perceived Impact of Social Media on Marital Relationships Among Gen Y And Z Students of Al-Hikmah University, Ilorin, Nigeria
text_snippet: Perceived Impact of Social Media on Marital Relationships Among Gen Y And Z Students of Al-Hikmah University, Ilorin, Nigeria The increasing integration of social media into daily life has raised concerns about its influence on the stability and quality of marital relationships. This study investigates the perceived impact of social media on marital relationships among Generation Y (Millennials) and Generation Z students at Al-Hikmah University in Nigeria. A qualitative research design was employed, involving semi-structured interviews with ten purposively selected participants from undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns in participants’ perceptions and experiences. Findings indicate that social media exerts a dual influence on marital dynamics, functioning both as a facilitator of communication and a source of relational strain. Positive effects include enhanced connectivity, particularly in long-distance relationships, and access to online resources for conflict resolution and counselling. Negative effects emerge from exposure to idealized portrayals of marriage, which contribute to unrealistic expectations, jealousy, mistrust, and dissatisfaction. title: From Tradition to Technology: Usage of AI Integration and Digital Informal Learning Among Islamic Teacher’s Functional Skills in Southern Pakistan
text_snippet: From Tradition to Technology: Usage of AI Integration and Digital Informal Learning Among Islamic Teacher’s Functional Skills in Southern Pakistan The digital divide and limited teacher readiness in rural areas remain major challenges in developing 21st-century teaching competencies. This study aims to examine the effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage and digital informal learning on the functional teaching skills of Islamic school teachers in rural Southern Pakistan. A quantitative approach was employed using a survey design involving 450 Islamic secondary school teachers in the Kot Addu district. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that AI usage has a significant positive effect on teachers’ functional skills, including communication, problem-solving, and instructional management. In contrast, digital informal learning does not show a statistically significant direct effect on functional skills. These results suggest that informal digital learning alone is insufficient to enhance teacher competencies without structured support and guided training. title: Project-based Learning to Enhance Higher-Order Thinking Skills: A Bibliometric Analysis for 21st-Century Education
text_snippet: Project-based Learning to Enhance Higher-Order Thinking Skills: A Bibliometric Analysis for 21st-Century Education The pedagogical approach that is considered effective in developing Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) is Project-Based Learning (PjBL). There is still a limited number of bibliometric analysis studies that specifically focus on the relevance of PjBL in the development of HOTs. This research aims to analyze bibliometrically the research development related to implementing PjBL to improve HOTS. Data were obtained from the Scopus database from 2015 to 2025, and analyzed using bibliometric analysis with the Vosviewer software. Results show a significant rise in publications related to PjBL and HOTS over the past decade, with Indonesia and other Asian countries contributing the most. Influential authors were identified through co-citation and bibliographic coupling, while collaboration patterns revealed predominantly local networks, indicating a need for stronger international partnerships. Keyword analysis highlights research emphasis on critical thinking development, technology integration in education, and innovative assessment methods. title: Enhancing Mathematical Dexterity of Eleventh Grade Humanities Students Through Social Media Videos
text_snippet: Enhancing Mathematical Dexterity of Eleventh Grade Humanities Students Through Social Media Videos Statistics and Probability are frequently perceived as abstract and challenging subjects, resulting in low engagement and academic performance, particularly among Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) students with limited mathematical orientation. This study investigates the effect of integrating curated social media video content on students’ academic performance and learning engagement. A mixed-methods action research design was employed involving 50 Grade 11 HUMSS students at Tunasan National High School. Data were collected through pre-test and post-test assessments, a Likert-scale perception questionnaire, and guided reflection journals. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. title: Understanding School Leadership in Elementary Schools Using Ordinal Correlation and K-Medians Clustering
text_snippet: Understanding School Leadership in Elementary Schools Using Ordinal Correlation and K-Medians Clustering School leadership plays a critical role in shaping instructional quality and institutional performance in elementary education. This study aims to examine school leaders’ competencies in leading, managing, and developing teachers in Hindang District, Leyte, Philippines, and to analyze the relationships among these competencies. A descriptive–correlational design was employed using complete enumeration of 121 elementary school teachers. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, and K-medians clustering. The findings indicate that school leaders are generally perceived as “very satisfactory” in leading (Median=4), managing (Median=4), and developing teachers (Median=4). Correlation analysis reveals significant positive relationships among the three competencies, indicating that effective leadership operates as an integrated system. title: Impact of Model Eliciting Activities in Geometry Learning: Anxiety, Self-Regulated Learning, and Learning Outcomes
text_snippet: Impact of Model Eliciting Activities in Geometry Learning: Anxiety, Self-Regulated Learning, and Learning Outcomes Low mathematics achievement and high mathematics anxiety in geometry among Indonesian students require innovative solutions. This study analyzes the effectiveness of Model Eliciting Activities (MEAs) in reducing mathematics anxiety, enhancing self-regulated learning (SRL), and improving students' geometry learning outcomes. Employing a quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design with 25 junior high school students in East Jakarta, validated and reliable instruments were used, including a mathematics anxiety questionnaire, an SRL questionnaire, and a geometry test. The research procedure involved a pretest, MEA implementation through four modeling stages, posttest, observation, and interviews. Data were analyzed using paired t-tests and multiple correlations. title: AN Experience of Wards from Divorced Family Living with Step-Parents among Student of Upper Basic School in Ilorin Metropolis
text_snippet: AN Experience of Wards from Divorced Family Living with Step-Parents among Student of Upper Basic School in Ilorin Metropolis Family structure transformation due to divorce and remarriage has raised concerns regarding children’s emotional and developmental well-being, as instability within stepfamily environments may expose children to psychological distress, inconsistent caregiving, and reduced academic engagement. This study aims to explore the lived experiences of upper basic school students from divorced families living with step-parents in Ilorin metropolis. A qualitative approach with a descriptive case study design was employed, involving ten participants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using semi-structured interviews and analyzed through thematic analysis. Findings reveal that students experience significant emotional distress, neglect, and instability, reflected in patterns of emotional abuse, deprivation of basic needs, and lack of parental support, with female students experiencing more severe maltreatment. Age differences indicate that younger students face direct forms of abuse, while older students experience indirect psychological burdens related to increased responsibilities. title: A A Case-Based Environmental Wisdom Learning Design for Developing Nature of Science and Environmental Awareness
text_snippet: A A Case-Based Environmental Wisdom Learning Design for Developing Nature of Science and Environmental Awareness Environmental degradation demands education that not only enhances scientific understanding but also fosters environmental awareness. However, research shows that prospective teachers still have naive conceptions of the Nature of Science (NOS) and low environmental awareness. title: Research Trends in Argumentation Skills in Indonesian Science Education: A Systematic Review of Models, Subjects, and Learning Topics
text_snippet: Research Trends in Argumentation Skills in Indonesian Science Education: A Systematic Review of Models, Subjects, and Learning Topics Argumentation skills are one of the important competencies of the 21st century that play a role in building conceptual understanding and critical thinking skills. This systematic literature review aims to analyze research trends (2020–2025) on learning models to improve argumentation skills in science education in Indonesia. The systematic review was conducted using the PRISMA method, utilizing two databases: Scopus and Google Scholar. Of the total 119 articles identified, 33 articles met the analysis criteria. The results show the dominance of the Argument Driven Inquiry (42%) and Problem-Based Learning (36%) models, which are mainly applied to high school students (73%) in the context of complex science topics. This review identified two crucial issues: a significant research gap at the junior high school level (12%) and persistent weaknesses among students in constructing high-level argument components, such as backing and rebuttal. These findings imply the need for further research at the junior high school level and the development of learning strategies that emphasize more complex argumentation training.

title: Perceptions of Non-Native English Speakers on English as the Global Lingua Franca: A Case Study
text_snippet: Perceptions of Non-Native English Speakers on English as the Global Lingua Franca: A Case Study Linguistic inequality has become an increasingly prominent global issue due to the dominance of English as a global lingua franca, which may marginalize non-native speakers and their native languages. This study aims to explore non-native English speakers’ perceptions of global English use, including its benefits, challenges, and implications for multilingualism. A qualitative case study design was employed. Participants consisted of nine non-native English speakers selected through purposive sampling from five countries: the Philippines, Indonesia, Japan, Sweden, and the United States. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that English functions as a key tool for global communication, academic access, and career advancement, while also presenting challenges such as accent bias, reduced confidence, and cultural displacement. Most participants perceived that English dominance reinforces linguistic inequality. The study highlights the importance of promoting multilingualism as a more inclusive approach to global communication. title: Cognitive Process Frameworks in Academic Writing: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Cognitive Process Frameworks in Academic Writing: A Systematic Review Academic writing poses significant challenges due to its complex cognitive processes. Research on cognitive processes in academic writing often lacks a clear and coherent theoretical framework, resulting in a fragmented and under-explored understanding of the cognitive processes employed in academic writing. The purpose of this study was to synthesize the dominant cognitive process frameworks and methodological approaches used in current academic writing research. This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the PRISMA protocol. A total of eleven articles met the inclusion criteria for further review. Data analysis was conducted using content analysis techniques with a thematic approach to present the relationships between findings in a descriptive and interpretive manner. The findings indicate that self-regulation and metacognition theories are the most frequently applied frameworks in modeling academic writing. Most studies employed qualitative methods, utilizing self-report instruments. The primary limitation identified was the narrow focus of studies on EFL learners. title: Making it Visible: A Scoping Review of a Competency Framework for ICT Literacy in Academic Writing
text_snippet: Making it Visible: A Scoping Review of a Competency Framework for ICT Literacy in Academic Writing Limited Integration of ICT literacy in academic writing remains a key challenge in a higher education. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive framework for ICT literacy using the Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes (KSA) model. A qualitative scoping review was conducted by analyzing 32 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Google Scholar, published between 2016 and 2025. Thematic analysis approach revealed nine key themes: source credibility evaluation, tool awareness, and digital ethics under the knowledge domain; digital research, academic writing with ICT, and collaborative writing under skills; and independent ICT use, adaptability to digital tools, and critical ICT awareness under attitudes. The findings show that students often struggle with evaluating sources, using tools reflectively, and understanding the ethical and epistemic impact of technology on their writing. title: Exploring the Challenges and Benefits of Culturally -Responsive Education in Nigeria: Bridging Tradition and Modernity in the Classroom
text_snippet: Exploring the Challenges and Benefits of Culturally -Responsive Education in Nigeria: Bridging Tradition and Modernity in the Classroom Culturally responsive education has gained increasing attention as a strategic approach to addressing diversity and promoting equity in higher education. Nigeria, characterized by complex cultural, linguistic, and social diversity, presents both opportunities and challenges for implementing culturally responsive pedagogy. Despite growing interest, comprehensive synthesis studies that systematically examine its implementation and implications remain limited. This study aims to analyze the challenges and opportunities of culturally responsive education in Nigeria and to explore its role in bridging tradition and modernity in classroom practices. A qualitative research design was employed using a systematic literature-based approach, drawing on peer-reviewed articles, policy documents, and relevant studies indexed in Scopus and Google Scholar. Thematic analysis identified six key dimensions: student engagement, diversity and inclusion, cultural competence, critical thinking, integration of indigenous knowledge, and implementation challenges. title: Bibliometric Analysis of Critical Thinking Skills in Higher Education (2015-2025): Trends, Collaborations, and Future Directions

title: Early Childhood Character Development: A Decade of Evidence from a Systematic Review of Educational Innovations and Barriers
text_snippet: Early Childhood Character Development: A Decade of Evidence from a Systematic Review of Educational Innovations and Barriers Character education development must begin at an early age by optimizing various learning strategies that align with contemporary challenges. One effective approach is to strengthen collaboration between teachers, parents, and the community. Therefore, the aim of this study is to analyze character development in early childhood and to examine the challenges and solutions that may arise during the process of character education development. This research employs a systematic literature review method, utilizing articles published between 2014 and 2024 from two reputable and credible databases: Scopus and Crossref. title: Cultivating Critical Consciousness: How Digital Media Reshapes Students’ Ethical Awareness in Anti-Corruption Education
text_snippet: Cultivating Critical Consciousness: How Digital Media Reshapes Students’ Ethical Awareness in Anti-Corruption Education Corruption remains a complex socio-political issue that undermines national governance and societal integrity. Anti-corruption education in higher education is expected to cultivate students' critical awareness and integrity in addressing such issues. However, the effectiveness of this education is often constrained by limitations in pedagogical approaches and delivery methods. This study aims to analyze the role of technology in enhancing students' critical awareness of social and political issues within the context of anti-corruption education. A qualitative case study approach was employed, with data collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis. The findings reveal that the use of digital platforms and social media significantly facilitates discourse, information dissemination, and the development of critical thinking among students. Nevertheless, barriers such as limited access to technology and low digital literacy remain persistent challenges.
